literal: Than poverty that which is painful what if one asks, than poverty poverty itself is that which is painful.
translation: If one asks what is as painful as poverty, the answer is that nothing is as painful as poverty itself.
modern: வறுமையை விடக் கொடுமையானது எது என்று கேட்டால், வறுமையை விட வறுமையே கொடுமையானது ஆகும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the incomparable suffering of poverty. The poet poses a rhetorical question asking what could possibly be more painful than being poor. By answering that only poverty itself is as painful as poverty, the verse emphasizes that no other misery in the world can match its devastating nature. The repetition of the words for poverty and pain reinforces the absolute and inescapable grip of destitution.
